replay_checkpoint() updates n_completed, n_hits, total_elapsed_s, and total_cost for completed cases. model_summary() computes avg_latency_s = total_elapsed_s / n_completed. EC2 test verified: 3 completed, 2 hits, cost 2.05, avg_latency 5.3s — all correct.
replay_checkpoint() returns None (no return statement, typed -> None). It does not call _check_rules(). Structurally impossible to produce a verdict.

In _run_model() lines 105-115: else branch calls create_run_folder() and write_run_config(). This is the original fresh-run path.
Line 146: `completed_keys.add(case.issue_key)` precedes line 148: `decision = monitor.update(model_id, result)`. The triggering case is tracked before any abort check.
Line 53 of run_monitor.py: `perf_min_cases: int = 10`. With 20 eval cases, performance floor fires at the halfway point (case 10).
pytest tests/ -q --tb=short → 310 passed in 20.10s. Zero failures.

warnings: Minor float drift in cost accumulation (e.g. 2.0500000000000003). Acceptable for dollar-level thresholds but could accumulate over hundreds of cases.

summary: All 8 acceptance criteria pass. The replay_checkpoint() method correctly rebuilds monitor state without triggering rules, model_dir reuse works via checkpoint, completed_keys ordering is correct, perf_min_cases is 10, and all 310 tests pass. Edge cases EC1-EC3 all verified with assertions. Three minor code quality warnings noted (float drift, checkpoint key semantics, typing) — none are blockers.
